name: cml-driver-eye
description: One lane of the CML output driver (design/cml_driver.sch) against the DR-0002 load -- 50 ohm/leg to the receiver's 3.3 V termination rail -- swept over pad capacitance 0/1/2 pF in-deck, at both spec/tmds-tx.md #1 operating points, across the full PVT matrix. Measures DR-0002's swing and common-mode rows, this stage's contribution to #2's <= 0.15 UI p-p jitter allocation, worst-case device stress against the 3.3 V devices' rated limit, and (unbounded by the ratified spec, reported for #9) 10-90 % rise/fall, tail-current draw and single-ended output resistance.
claim: spec/tmds-tx.md#dr-0002 -- single-ended swing 400-600 mV and common mode 2.8-3.3 V into 50 ohm/leg with a ~10 mA tail, plus the Vgs/Vgd/Vds margin against the 3.3 V core devices' rated limit that DR-0002 explicitly deferred to the driver design work -- and spec/tmds-tx.md #2's remaining-jitter row, this stage's <= 0.15 UI peak-to-peak allocation, at both #1 operating points (742.5 Mbps/lane target, 270 Mbps/lane fallback).

transient.pattern: mixed-run-length-16b (1111111110101010, MSB first at t=0): a nine-bit run followed by maximum-transition-density alternation, so both the settled-history and the worst-case-ISI edge cases are excited by one pattern

swing_c0.description: DR-0002 single-ended swing 400-600 mV, 0 pF pad. Measured on one leg as (max high level - min low level) over the mid-bit sampling comb (central 40 % of each bit) of the maximum-transition-density section only: the DC-settled nine-bit run is excluded, so this is the dynamic eye height a receiver slices, not the DC swing (reported separately as swing_dc) and not the switching peak-to-peak excursion (reported separately as vpp_c0).

swing_c1.description: DR-0002 single-ended swing 400-600 mV, 1 pF pad

swing_c2.description: DR-0002 single-ended swing 400-600 mV at DR-0005's full 2 pF pad-capacitance budget

vcm_c0.description: DR-0002 common mode 2.8-3.3 V, 0 pF pad; (Vhigh+Vlow)/2 averaged over both legs, at the nominal 3.3 V receiver termination rail DR-0002's absolute window is referenced to (avcc -10 %/+10 % sensitivity is reported separately as vcm_avcclo/vcm_avcchi)

vcm_c1.description: DR-0002 common mode 2.8-3.3 V, 1 pF pad

vcm_c2.description: DR-0002 common mode 2.8-3.3 V at DR-0005's full 2 pF pad-capacitance budget

dj_ui_c0.description: spec/tmds-tx.md #2 remaining-jitter row: this stage's <= 0.15 UI peak-to-peak allocation, 0 pF pad. Deterministic jitter only (ISI + rise/fall asymmetry), measured as the peak-to-peak spread of the input-to-output crossing delay over the pattern's edge set and normalised by the measured UI; the input is jitter-free by construction, so the whole spread is contributed here. Random jitter is not a transient quantity and is not included -- see the record.

dj_ui_c2.description: spec/tmds-tx.md #2 remaining-jitter row at DR-0005's full 2 pF pad-capacitance budget

dj_ui_cmis.description: spec/tmds-tx.md #2 remaining-jitter row with a deliberate 1 pF leg-to-leg pad-capacitance mismatch (2 pF on OUTP, 1 pF on OUTN) -- half of DR-0005's whole budget as imbalance. Graded against the same allocation because a pad ring that lands inside DR-0005's budget but mismatched must still close the jitter row; this is the row that turns 'the legs must match' into a number for the pad/ESD work.

swing_cmis.description: DR-0002 swing under the same 1 pF leg-to-leg pad mismatch

vgs_sw_max.description: Switching-device Vgs against the 3.3 V core devices' rated terminal voltage. 3.63 V (nominal + 10 %) is adopted as the rated ceiling -- the same envelope this repo's own mandated PVT matrix already treats as the supply extreme (sim/harness/corners.py DEFAULT_SUPPLY_TOLERANCE), and the standard reliability convention for a device family whose own characterization bias is Vgs=Vds=3.3V nominal (GF180MCU PDK Electrical Specifications Sec.1.0, 'Low Voltage Devices (3.3V)', https://gf180mcu-pdk.readthedocs.io/en/latest/analog/spice/elec_specs/elec_specs_1.html -- Idsat characterized at |Vds|=|Vgs|=3.3V; no separate absolute-maximum-rating table ships with the volare distribution). The device's hard breakdown ceiling is far above this: the same table's punch-through voltage BVDSS is 7-9 V (NCH) / -6.5 to -8.5 V (PCH), so 3.63 V is a rated-operating margin choice, not a proximity-to-breakdown one. Measured on the avcc +10 % copy, the worst-case termination rail.

vgd_sw_max.description: Switching-device |Vgd| against the same 3.63 V rated limit -- the binding stress row, since the off device's gate sits at the multiplexer's low level while its drain is pulled to the termination rail

vds_sw_max.description: Switching-device Vds against the same 3.63 V rated limit

vgs_tail_max.description: Tail/mirror-device Vgs (the shared bias node) against the same 3.63 V rated limit

vds_tail_max.description: Tail-device Vds (the tail node) against the same 3.63 V rated limit; also the switching devices' source-bulk reverse bias, since every bulk is tied to VSS

itail_dc.description: Tail current from the ideal 500 uA reference through the cell's 1:20 mirror. The 8-12 mA window is the tail-current tolerance this cell requires of the follow-on bias network, derived in design/cml-driver-sizing.md from DR-0002's 400-600 mV swing window; checking it here makes that derived requirement a graded row rather than a note.

ui_ref.description: Harness-integrity check, not a design claim: the measured unit interval must differ by more than 50 % across the grid, which it can only do if rate_val actually reached the stimulus. A flat ui_ref would mean the bit-rate axis silently failed to apply and every jitter number was normalised by the wrong UI.
